problems.claim: Segment 0xFAE3A2 evidence: "192 LE32 slots inside the span, 88 of them the 0xFFFFFFFF 'no handler' marker the reader tests at 0xFADB69".
problems.problem: The count is 116, not 88. Read straight from original_ROMs/wsa1_prom_a.ic12: of the 192 slots at 0xFAE3A2, 116 are 0xFFFFFFFF and 76 hold real in-span targets (pointing at only 14 distinct handlers). No mode of prom_a_fad800_layout.py prints 88 -- not --tables, not --selftest, not the default report -- so this is a quantified claim reproduced by no script AND contradicted by the ROM. It is the same shape as this project's recorded 'a handler count of 35 that was 34'. The segment boundary itself (768 bytes, 192 entries) is correct and independently confirmed, and the table really is sparse, so the structural conclusion survives -- but the number must be corrected to 116 empty / 76 filled before any of this prose reaches a routine header.

problems.claim: Verdict: "Module 1 ... and module 2 ... are ordinary dispatched code with 19 inline jump tables between them plus a 192-entry sparse handler table at 0xFAE3A2".
problems.problem: There are 18, not 19. The layout has 21 pointer_table segments; removing the 192-entry dispatch table at 0xFAE3A2 and the two 33-entry blob tables (0xFAF7E8, 0xFB0700) leaves 18 -- ten in module 1 (0xFADBA9, 0xFADCBE, 0xFADD77, 0xFADDA0, 0xFADDC1, 0xFADDF1, 0xFADF77, 0xFAE04D, 0xFAE28F, 0xFAE30E) and eight in module 2 (0xFAE802, 0xFAE82A, 0xFAE9D0, 0xFAEDF0, 0xFAEE5C, 0xFAF16C, 0xFAF410, 0xFAF6B8). Related: the committed script's own docstring says "a linear decode ... desynchronises inside the first module -- there are eight inline jump tables in it", and module 1 has ten.

problems.claim: Segment 0xFADD87-0xFADD9F evidence: "accept()-promoted run 0xFADD89-0xFADDA9".
problems.problem: --accepted prints 0xFADD89-0xFADD9F, 23 bytes. The quoted upper bound 0xFADDA9 runs 10 bytes past the segment and straight through the pointer_table at 0xFADDA0-0xFADDA7, which the same dossier frames as a segment. The segment boundary is right; the cited range is not.

problems.claim: Segment 0xFADDC9-0xFADDF0 evidence: "entries of the table at 0xFADDC1 plus accept()-promoted 0xFADDCA-0xFADDF0".
problems.problem: --accepted lists no promoted run anywhere in 0xFADDC9-0xFADDF0; its 26 runs are 0xFAD801, 0xFAD806, 0xFAD819, 0xFAD846, 0xFAD86C, 0xFAD886, 0xFAD89D, 0xFAD8B8, 0xFAD8D9, 0xFAD8FA, 0xFAD98B, 0xFAD9AC, 0xFAD9C7, 0xFADD89, 0xFADF0D, 0xFAE02E, 0xFAE049, 0xFAE2DE, 0xFAE823, 0xFAE84B, 0xFAE861, 0xFAEA11, 0xFAEBAB, 0xFAEC79, 0xFAED7D, 0xFB19E8. The segment is actually BETTER evidenced than claimed (both entries of table 0xFADDC1 are 0xFADDC9 and 0xFADDCA, so it is pure descent), but the stated fact is false.

problems.claim: Reclist A evidence: "Targets 0x7F32..0x7F3C step 1, LAST record (index 10, 0xFB1A74) = 0x7F3C".
problems.problem: Index 10 is at 0xFB1A3E + 10*6 = 0xFB1A7A, whose target is 0x7F3C. 0xFB1A74 is index 9, target 0x7F3B. The value quoted is right and the list really does run 0x7F32..0x7F3C on 11 records (verified record by record from the ROM); only the address of the last record is off by one record.

problems.claim: Segment 0xFADBD9 evidence "entry [0] of the table at 0xFADBA9", and segment 0xFADD87 evidence "entry [0] of the table at 0xFADD77".
problems.problem: In both tables entry[0] is 0xFAE2E2, not the segment start. Table 0xFADBA9 = [0xFAE2E2, 0xFADBD9, 0xFADBD9, 0xFADC20, 0xFADC42, 0xFADC7E x7]; table 0xFADD77 = [0xFAE2E2, 0xFADD87, 0xFADD87, 0xFADD88]. The correct citations are entry[1]/[2] in each case. The segment starts ARE table entries, so the layout is unaffected.

problems.claim: Segment 0xFAD800 evidence: "descent from thunk targets T_F40860->0xFAD800, T_F4085C->0xFAD805, T_F40858->0xFAD80A and 12 more"; segment 0xFADE01 evidence: "descent from thunk targets T_F40890->0xFADE8D and T_F40894->0xFADF08".
problems.problem: Off-by-one and an omission. Recomputed from the prom_b thunk directory: 16 thunk targets land in 0xFAD800-0xFADBA8, so after naming three it is "13 more", not 12. And 0xFADE01-0xFADF76 contains THREE thunk targets, not two -- T_F40854->0xFADF1E is missing from the list. The 33-slot total is still exactly right (16+3+1+1+1+4+4+2+1 = 33).

problems.claim: Segment 0xFAE822-0xFAE829 evidence: "eight 0x0E bytes that are the targets of the table at 0xFAE802".
problems.problem: Only six of the eight are targets of that table (0xFAE822, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28). 0xFAE823 is not referenced by it at all -- it is one of the 26 accept()-promoted runs -- and 0xFAE829 is reached from thunk T_F41F3C and calr 0xfae829 at 0xFAE857, not from the table. The bytes really are eight 0x0E, verified.

problems.claim: Verdict: "Between module 2's code and module 3 sits a 10.5 KiB parameter store ... each framing ~3.5 KiB of 4-byte records".
problems.problem: 0xFAF7A6 (first byte after module 2's code) to 0xFB1800 (module 3) is 8,282 bytes = 8.1 KiB, of which 7,150 bytes (7.0 KiB) are the maps, pointer tables and blobs and 1,132 are pad. Even taking it to the end of the span it is 10,330 bytes = 10.1 KiB. And blob 2 is 3,088 bytes = 3.0 KiB, which "~3.5 KiB" overstates (blob 1 is 3,732 = 3.6 KiB).

problems.claim: notes/prom_a_fad800_layout.py's docstring: "26 code runs totalling ~306 bytes (~4%) are accept()-promoted".
problems.problem: The script's own --accepted prints "26 runs, 261 bytes (3.7% of the 7107 code bytes)". The docstring of the one committed artefact disagrees with the artefact's output by 45 bytes. The dossier itself quotes the correct 261/3.7%, so this is a defect in the script that must be fixed before the coordinator commits it.

problems.claim: notes/prom_a_fad800_layout.py's docstring: "notes/prom_a_module_frontier.py ranks it top by contiguous unconverted extent summed over the thunk runs that point into it".
problems.problem: Summed, this span's runs give 3216 + 2595 + 0 = 5,811. The 0xFA5AEB-0xFAA000 span's runs (T_F43350 8,886; T_F40744 7,668; T_F40714 245) sum to 16,799, and T_F43350 alone outranks anything here -- prom_a_module_frontier.py --n 20 puts this span's runs at ranks 4, 6 and 13. The span IS prom_a's largest remaining .incbin (18,432 B), which is what WAVE7-BRIEFING.md says and is a perfectly good justification; the frontier-summed claim is not. The dossier does not repeat this claim, only the script does.

problems.claim: Summary: "this is the ONLY place the layout is wrong and it is 6 + ~48 bytes".
problems.problem: Stronger than the method supports. --tablebases finds unframed data only where DECODED CODE loads the base as a 32-bit immediate; a byte table reached through a 16-bit address, an lda, or a pointer already in RAM would be invisible to it, and --selftest asserting "the list is exactly these two" only pins that route. My own independent sweep for constant-byte runs >= 6 inside code segments found nothing beyond 0xFADD30's zero runs and the legitimate 8 x 0x0E stub block, which supports the claim -- but "ONLY" should be "the only one this method can see".

problems.claim: --selftest is the artefact that re-proves the layout.
problems.problem: Robustness nit found by mutation testing: when a PTRBLOB stops qualifying, selftest() prints the FAIL for 'PTRBLOB count' and then dies with an uncaught IndexError at notes/prom_a_fad800_layout.py:930 (`b0 = [b for b in blobs if b[0] == 0xFAF7E8][0]`), so the remaining ~40 checks never run and the failure summary is never printed. Exit status is still non-zero, so nothing is silently passed, but a future lane debugging a moved boundary gets a traceback instead of a report.

lanes.verifier_verdict:
SURVIVES VERIFICATION on every load-bearing claim, with one wrong number that must be corrected before the prose is reused.

What I could not break. The script notes/prom_a_fad800_layout.py exists, runs, and every one of its twelve documented modes prints what the dossier says it prints; --selftest is 57 checks / 0 failures / exit 0. I did not take the selftest on trust: I imported the module, poisoned its ROM cache one byte at a time, and confirmed it FAILS on the very LAST byte of the span (0xFB1FFF), on the LAST entry of blob table 0xFAF7E8, and on the LAST record target of reclist C. The last-element checks bite.

I re-derived the load-bearing numbers with my own code and with a different disassembler. Tiling: 63 segments, every printed length equals hi-lo+1, gapless, no overlaps, first at 0xFAD800, last ends 0xFB1FFF, sum exactly 18,432; 7,107 + 9,526 + 1,790 + 9 = 18,432. Null corpus: re-implemented from the docstring, 10,509 runs / 287,291 bytes identical, and I additionally proved the corpus is real by byte-checking all 109,819 instruction comments against the ROM (0 mismatches) and confirming 0 runs overlap the span. Independently re-implemented PTRTAB>=2/window=span (0 FP), IDENT>=12 (0 FP) and IDENT>=8 (5 FP at the same addresses). All 21 code segments re-decoded with unidasm rather than llvm-mc: all 21 consume exactly, tile internally, and end in ret/jp/jr. The 183 published entry points recomputed from the two ROM images: 150 distinct in-span table entries + 33 thunk targets, 117 in code + 66 in blob, zero off an instruction boundary. All 33 thunk slots read out of wsa1_prom_b.ic13 land in the span and in code segments.

Citations are clean. I spot-checked well over twenty cited addresses, not three, and every single one is at the INSTRUCTION address, not one past it. The index-map loaders are the sharpest case: the 4-byte immediates sit at 0xFAED54/0xFAEF55/... while the dossier cites 0xFAED53/0xFAEF54/..., i.e. the 0x44/0x45 opcodes -- exactly the off-by-one this project was burned by, and it is right here. The two negative claims also hold under a real census: zero occurrences of 0x00FAE802 / 0x00FAE82A anywhere in ALL FOUR images, and 0xFADD60 has no 24-bit reference, no 32-bit reference, and no jr/jrl encoding anywhere in the span that could reach it. "Nothing in the span is ASCII" is stronger than stated: the longest printable run is 6 bytes. No KN5000 name is borrowed, so no byte diff was owed.

The one thing that does not survive. The Evidence line for the dispatch table at 0xFAE3A2 says "88 of them the 0xFFFFFFFF 'no handler' marker". It is 116 (76 filled slots, hitting only 14 distinct handlers). No mode of the script prints 88 and the ROM contradicts it. The table's extent, its 192-entry count, its reader bound and its sparseness all stand -- but the number is the same failure the error list already records as "a handler count of 35 that was 34", and a converting lane would copy it into a routine header. Fix it to 116 empty / 76 filled.

Around that sit eleven small slips, all in prose rather than in the layout: 19 inline jump tables that are 18; two accept()-promoted ranges quoted wrong (0xFADD89-0xFADDA9 is really -0xFADD9F, and the 0xFADDCA-0xFADDF0 run does not exist); reclist A's last record at 0xFB1A74 when index 10 is 0xFB1A7A; two "entry [0]" citations that are entry [1]; "and 12 more" thunk targets that are 13, plus T_F40854->0xFADF1E omitted from 0xFADE01's list; "eight targets" of table 0xFAE802 that are six; a 10.5 KiB parameter store that is 8.1 KiB; and, in the committed script itself, a docstring that says ~306 bytes where its own --accepted says 261 and a frontier-ranking justification that does not survive running the frontier. None of them moves a boundary. All of them should be corrected before the coordinator commits notes/prom_a_fad800_layout.py -- which is still untracked, exactly as the dossier warned.

Hygiene: prom_a/wsa1_prom_a.s, prom_b, prom_c and prom_d are untouched; git diff --stat is empty; HEAD is still 65da9d2; and scripts/analysis/assert_byte_identical.py prints "PASS: every rebuilt ROM is byte-identical."

dossier.verdict: THREE CODE MODULES SEPARATED BY TWO LARGE DATA ZONES; it is 39% code by byte. Module 1 (0xFAD800-0xFAE3A0) and module 2 (0xFAE800-0xFAF7A5) are ordinary dispatched code with 19 inline jump tables between them plus a 192-entry sparse handler table at 0xFAE3A2 whose bound its own reader states (`cp A,0xbf` at 0xFADB55). Between module 2's code and module 3 sits a 10.5 KiB parameter store: two 33-entry pointer tables (0xFAF7E8 stride 0x74, 0xFB0700 stride 0x60), each framing ~3.5 KiB of 4-byte records that a copy loop streams into 0x60F330 until a record whose first byte is 0xFF, plus two 33-byte 0..0x1F index maps at 0xFAF7A6/0xFAF7C7 that six and four instructions respectively load. Module 3 (0xFB1800-0xFB1A3D, the single T_F40840 slot) is a REGISTER-POKE ENGINE: three routines each fetch a list base from a one-entry pointer slot and walk a record array applying mem[addr] = (mem[addr] & and) | or; the arrays are 11x6, 32x6 and 32x28 bytes and their targets are RAM/IO 0x7F32-0x7F3C and thirty-two 0x40-byte blocks based at 0x76AE / 0x76CD with array index 8 skipped. Nothing in the span is ASCII; 1,799 bytes are padding or alignment. Every byte is accounted for with ZERO `unknown` runs and ZERO barrier conflicts, but the layout carries one stated hole: two BYTE tables (0xFADA20, 0xFADD30) sit inside `code` segments, because the content rules find pointer tables and a byte table is indistinguishable from instructions by shape.

open_questions: 0xF86B88-0xF86B8C decodes uniquely as `ld XIY,0x00f86bb8` and falls into the shared tail at 0xF86B8D, but a census of the 3-byte LE address 0xF86B88 over both images returns ZERO hits. The extent of the word table at 0xF86C8C is 34 bytes (17 entries) only because the next PROVEN code byte is 0xF86CAE and nothing references 0xF86CAA. Its reader (`ld WA,(XHL+WA)` at 0xF86C78, index = (0x2096)<<1) has NO bound instruction, so 15 entries + a separate 4-byte object at 0xF86CAA is not excluded -- only made unattractive by the zero-reference census. The three large zero fields (951 B at 0xF872CA, 783 B at 0xF87B72, 699 B at 0xF893B6) plus the 391/438/20/16/12/21-byte ones are labelled `pad` purely because they are uniform 0x00. Block A measures exactly 0x800 from directory base to fallback list and block B exactly 0x1000, but block C measures 0x7B0, so the 'fixed block size' reading does not survive its own last case.
The single 0xFF at 0xF89685, 0x14 bytes past the fallback list at 0xF89671, is unexplained and unreferenced.

What the record fields MEAN is only partly pinned. id (byte +0) is the directory index, 0..191, proven by `cp L,0xbf`. tag (byte +1) indexes the 1<<k table at 0xF8671A to set/clear a bit in the 64-bit word at (0x2088)/(0x208C), so it is a small subsystem/group number. value (+2) and mask (+3) are ANDed together at 0xF8666A. Callers pass W=0x7F (a 7-bit mask) and D=0x00/0x05/0x06. I have NOT established what a given id number denotes, so I propose no name containing the word 'MIDI' or a controller number.

0xF868DB's 32-byte sign-magnitude curve (-7..+7) and 0xF868FB's 8-byte 0,1,4,10,20,50,70,100 have their extents from 'next table base' / 'next code byte' only -- neither has a reader bound. Whether the two index spaces of the 0xF86EC1 handler table (0..0x2F from 0xF86EC1, 0..0xDF from entry 32) are meant to overlap on entries 32-47, or whether one bound is a firmware bug, is not established.

dossier.summary: A conversion lane should: (1) run `python3 notes/prom_a_f85ff9_layout.py --python` and take the 45-segment LAYOUT verbatim -- every byte assigned, contiguous, 0 barrier conflicts, checked by `--selftest` (82 checks, 0 failed, and it checks the LAST segment, the LAST entry of each 192-entry directory and the LAST entry of the 256-entry table, not only the first); (2) emit code with `python3 prom_a/roundtrip.py LO HI --block` per code segment and splice with `prom_a/insert_region.py`; (3) emit the pointer_table/list_area segments as `.long`, the index_map/bit_table segments as `.byte`/`.long`, and the pad segments as `.fill` ONLY where every byte really is one value (the script's `pad` kind already guarantees that). (4) BEFORE writing any header, re-run `--selftest`: the numbers in this report are its output, not a reader's addition. Names I would propose, each with the Evidence line the header must carry: ChangeQueue_Post_Buf2C00 (0xF86A81 -- appends {DE,WA} at 0x2C00 + index (0x60F000), caps the index at 0xFB, writes the 0xFF end marker at +4, index += 4); ChangeQueue_Post (0xF86AA3 -- the same for 0x2E00/(0x60F004); 58 proven call sites); ChangeQueue_Post_Slot (0xF86AC7 -- scans 0x2030..0x206B for the first 0xFF slot); ChangeQueue_Flip (0xF860A6 -- `ldirw` 0x2E00 -> 0x2C00 for (0x60F004)>>1 words, terminates 0x2C00, zeroes (0x60F004)); ChangeQueue_Run (0xF869DB -- the drain loop; id bound `cp L,0xbf`, directory lookup id<<2, per-entry `call T,XDE` over a 0xFFFFFFFF-terminated list, then the fallback list at (0x20C4)); ChangeQueue_RunA/B/C (0xF8697E/0xF8699D/0xF869BC -- each installs a (directory, fallback list, queue base) triple into (0x20C0)/(0x20C4)/(0x20AD) then `calr 0xF869DB`); Handler_NullStub (0xF872C1). I would NOT name the ids, the tag byte, or the value curves -- see open_questions. THREE THINGS TO CARRY OUT OF THIS LANE THAT ARE NOT ABOUT THIS SPAN. (a) scripts/analysis/trace_code.py's is_flow_end() has a BUG: it tests conditions against `NZ|Z|NC|C|PO|PE|P|M|NV|V|GE|LT|GT|LE|UGE|ULT|UGT|ULE|F`, but MAME's s_cond[16] (../mame/src/devices/cpu/tlcs900/dasm900.cpp:1409-1411) spells four of them with a slash -- PE/OV, M/MI, PO/NOV, P/PL -- so every descent built on that file reads `jr PE/OV,...` as UNCONDITIONAL and stops dead. In this span alone it cost two runs (0xF86B52, 0xF86B64) that are ordinary fall-through code. I did NOT fix trace_code.py (another lane owns it); my script overrides is_flow_end() locally with the correction cited to the MAME table. (b) prom_a/wsa1_prom_a.s currently emits THREE computed-jump tables as instructions: 0xF9CEE6, 0xFA0487 and 0xFE1551, each 5 entries, each sitting immediately after its own `add XBC,imm32 / ld XBC,(XBC) / jp (xbc)` reader whose immediate is the table address (readers at 0xF9CEDC, 0xFA047D, 0xFE1547). `--misframed` finds 29 sites of that shape and marks these 3. notes/prom_a_jumptables.py reports 13 tables and finds none of the three -- it matches the OTHER spelling, `jp T,XBC`. (c) the same tool's blind spot means any null corpus taken from prom_a's proven instruction text is contaminated: ~2,400 bytes of `nop`/`ret` padding, ~215 bytes of blank-fill and one credit string are transcribed as instructions. Quote raw counts and adjudicate, as `--null` now does.

BUT the dossier carries eight errata, four of them serious, and all four are in the exact class this project's error list is made of: uncorroborated prose counts, none checked by the 79-check selftest. (1) "ten of its eleven objects are named" is NINE - the lane's own DATA_READERS has None for two, and the sentence is the one that carries the whole provenance argument. dossier.question: Gap A's last four 0x0010C000 per-channel registers — 0x0440, 0x0480, 0x04C0, 0x0500: locate every write, trace the value back, state the range/clamp, and name them only where the evidence carries it.
dossier.answer:
## Headline

**0x0440, 0x0480 and 0x04C0 are not scalars. Their low 6–7 bits are a 0x0010C000 CHANNEL NUMBER** — the very number the same routine hands, a few instructions later, to a `Dev10C_Slot*` accessor as that accessor's `chan` argument, where it becomes the register selector `chan + 0x0580/0x0600` (slot 2), `chan + 0x05C0/0x0640` (slot 3) or `chan + 0x0540/0x01C0` (slot 1) on the same device. They are **channel cross-references**: register `0x0440 + n` on channel n holds channel m. The remaining bits are a 2-bit field from the DSP algorithm descriptor (0x0440/0x0480) or a 6-bit tone-record field plus two constant bits (0x04C0).

**0x0500 is different in kind**: a byte pair, each half independently clamped to `[0, 0x7F]`, with a second producer the shipped census could not see.

★ **A fourth register joins the family, outside the assigned four**: `0x0180 + chan` — the one the sibling note called "pan" — carries the **slot-1 channel in bits 13..8**, built by the identical idiom from the identical allocator. That names the "high-byte flags sub_FA9C60 accumulates in (XIZ+0xfa)" that `FINDINGS-prom_c-dev10c-sibling-register-map.md` §4 left unexplained. It does not disturb the pan reading of the low seven bits; the ROM's own reset image agrees with both halves (word 6 = `0x0040` = the sibling's stated pan centre, with a zero high byte).

## Per register

| reg | value | allowed bits | clamp / rejection |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x0440` | `(tone2[+0x1E] & 0x00C0) \| chan` (path A) or `AlgoFlags \| (chan & 0x7F)` (path B, class 13) | `0x00FF` | channel rejected unless `< 0x80`; word cleared at `0xFA991C` |
| `0x0480` | `AlgoFlags \| (chan & 0x3F)` (class 12) | `0x00FF` | rejected unless `< 0x80`; word cleared at `0xFA9923` |
| `0x04C0` | `0x4400 \| (tone2[+0x22] & 0x3300) \| (chan & 0x7F)` | `0x777F` | rejected unless `< 0x80`; ⚠ **seeded 0x4400, NOT cleared** — a rejected slot 3 leaves `0x4400` |
| `0x0500` | `(hi << 8) \| lo`, both clamped `[0,0x7F]`; or, when bit 9 of `voice[+0x01]` is set, `sub_FC7FCA`'s `byte<<8`/`byte<<9` high byte with only the low byte OR'd in | `0x7F7F` on the A/B path | `Clamp_ToRange_Word` (0xFA7598), bounds `0x0000`/`0x007F` |
| *(bonus)* `0x0180` | `(tone2[+0x20] & 0xC000) \| (slot-1 chan << 8) \| pan(0..0x7F)` | `0xFF7F` | slot-1 channel rejected unless `< 0x40`; high byte then stays 0 |

**The 2-bit field is DSP-derived.** `sub_FB5E39` returns exactly `0x00C0`, `0x0040` or `0x0000` (`ld WA,imm16` occurs exactly twice in its 344 bytes) after indexing `DSP_AlgoDescriptor_Records` at `0xFDF4F1` as `base + 39*algotype + 19 + 5*d` — the 12×39 table already named in `FINDINGS-prom_c-voice-tables.md` §2, with 39 = 19-byte header + four 5-byte sub-records.

**Where the channel comes from.** `sub_FA5ED3` is an allocator returning `(class << 8) | handle`, `0xFF` = none; `sub_FA598C` maps handle→channel by a group taken from the ROM table at `0xFE10C9`. Four RAM arrays close on one another exactly: `0x0AA8 + 27*34 = 0x0E3E`, `0x0E3E + 5*192 = 0x11FE`, `0x11FE + 12*64 = 0x14FE`, and `0x4CCF + 27*128 = 0x5A4F` (the key-zone tuning word the pitch chain already uses). 192 handles = 0xC0, which is also the not-allocated sentinel.

**Three parallel groups, one per hardware slot.** `sub_FA9915` (slot 2, `tone2[+0x1E]`, tone-object `0x59+4k`, `0x4CCF` sub-record +0), `sub_FA9C60` (slot 1, `+0x20`, `0x69+4k`, +9), `sub_FA9F19` (slot 3, `+0x22`, `0x79+4k`, +18) — three consecutive u16s, three tone-object bases 0x10 apart, three 9-byte sub-records tiling the 27-byte stride.

## Names proposed

**None for 0x0440/0x0480/0x04C0/0x0500.** The KN5000 leaves 0x440 and 0x480 unnamed in its own register table too. What *is* proposed, and carried by the evidence, is a **type**: "channel cross-reference, low 6–7 bits, in this device's 0..0x7F slot-extended encoding, with the rest a small field". That is exactly the deliverable shape the brief asked for over a confident wrong name.

## The sibling: structural, not a transplant

The KN5000 sub-CPU has the same routine writing the same registers with the **same class constants**: `Voice_Chan_Fallback_NoWaveTable` calls `DSP_AlgoType_Dispatch3(de=1)`, then `ExtVoice_Alloc_StreamSlot(de=0xD)` = class **13**, tests `>= 0x80`, calls `NoteState_ClearRecord`, masks `0x7F`, stores to `0x0451DC` (TG reg **0x440**); `Voice_Chan_SecondaryPitch_Trigger` does it with `de=0` and class **12** into `0x0451DE` (TG reg **0x480**). The sibling's own comments call these "a precomputed slot word" and "the secondary slot word". Its allocator's prologue is the same algorithm — `and 0x3F` on the class, bound `0x40` on arg1, `(class<<8)|0xFF` on failure — with a different part bound (0x1A = 26 there, 0x21 = 33 here).

**Byte diffs, all four pairs**: 336/339, 252/256, **55/63**, 164/168 different. Nothing is transplanted.

⚠ One WSA1/KN5000 difference worth recording: the WSA1 masks 0x0480's channel to **6 bits** (`and BC,0x003f`, 0xFA9BC2) where the KN5000 keeps the full 7.

## What I corrected

`notes/prom_c_gapA_remaining_regs.py` already existed, untracked, when this lane started (mtime 20:21, five minutes before my first command — presumably an earlier run of this same lane). I re-derived every claim in it from the ROM independently and **found three defects**:

1. **A false quantified claim guarded by a test that cannot fail.** §10 printed "all four pairs differ in more than **90%**" and verified it with `check(True, True)`. The third pair is **87.3% (55 of 63)**. Replaced with a computed floor that names the pair setting it.
2. **An over-generalisation.** The docstring said the register is "left cleared" when the lookup answers 0xFF. True for 0x0440/0x0480; **false for 0x04C0**, which is seeded `0x4400` at `0xFA9F20` before any test.
3. **A negative control that contradicted its own label** ("the 0x3300 and 0x4400 fields would NOT tile with a 0x00FF channel", asserting that they *do*). Replaced, plus two new controls.

And I added: §3b (0x0180's high byte), §9d (range/clamp table, every mask read back out of the ROM at the operand position it claims), a `SIB_BASE` guard against the off-by-0xEB00 splice bug this project has already paid for, a residue-0 completeness check that the `add rr,imm16` opcode filter loses nothing inside the driver banks, and a proof that `sub_FA96F7` calls neither allocator in either call form.

Final state: **16 sections, 64 assertions, 8 negative controls, FAILURES: 0**, exit 0. `assert_byte_identical.py` → `PASS: every rebuilt ROM is byte-identical.` No `.s` file touched (`git diff --stat -- prom_a prom_b prom_c prom_d` is empty).

open_questions: WHY does one channel name another? 'Modulator', 'partner partial', 'effect-send target' and 'the stream the sample is read from' all fit a channel-valued register and nothing in prom_c distinguishes them. What is measured is that the value IS a channel number in this device's own 0..0x7F slot-extended encoding.

What do 0x04C0's two constant bits (0x4400) mean? They are a literal seeded at routine entry and never varied. Likewise the meaning of the 6-bit tone-record field 0x3300 and of the 2-bit DSP-descriptor field 0x00C0/0x0040.

The 192-entry handle array at RAM 0x0E3E (5 bytes each, ending exactly at 0x11FE) is 3 x 64, which matches 64 channels x 3 slots — but that factorisation is an OBSERVATION, not proven. 0xC0 is independently the not-allocated sentinel tested at 0xFA5F37.

Why is the per-channel bookkeeping array at 0x4CCF indexed by the channel (0..0x7F) AND subdivided into three 9-byte sub-records, when the 0..0x7F channel encoding already distinguishes slot 1 from slot 3? Either the index is not exactly the channel, or the sub-records are per-slot state kept redundantly.

0x0500's high byte on the sub_FC7FCA path is byte(0x00E17C+part) shifted 8 or 9 — the << 9 arm can set bit 15, which the Voice_StageRegs_0500_08C0_AB path never does. Nothing bounds that RAM byte from the ROM, so 0x0500's true upper range on that path is not established.

0x0500's LOW half is sub_FA75BA(tone[+0x48], voice[+0x0C], 6) + 0x7F clamped to [0,0x7F] — an offset of +127 into a ceiling of 127, so every non-negative input saturates. That asymmetry is read off the instructions (0xFA95F9 add HL,0x007f) and is not explained here.
Whether 0x0180's high byte and low byte are ONE quantity to the hardware. They are assembled by an `or` of two independently computed halves; only the bit positions are measured.

The select-site census recognises `add rr,imm16` only. Inside the two driver banks that is proven lossless (residue 0), but a selector built some other way OUTSIDE the banks would be invisible, so 'there is no path into these registers that does not go through the staged word' is a scan result, not a proof.
